heroHeadline: Venezuela Frees 39 Political Prisoners as Post-Maduro Transition Talks Yield Tangible Results
heroSubtitle: Venezuela released 39 political prisoners on September 27 following the second round of post-Maduro transition talks, a tangible outcome of negotiations focused on democratic normalization. The releases came a day after government and opposition delegations agreed to establish a panel to review Supreme Tribunal of Justice candidate selection — the first concrete judicial-reform step since the January capture of Maduro. Foro Penal had counted 344 political prisoners as of September 14, down from 391 in late August; the 39 new releases signal continued, if gradual, progress. Earlier in the week, President Trump and interim President Delcy Rodríguez met at the UN General Assembly on September 23 and Chevron's $7B+ joint-venture deal remains in place as inflation eased to an 18-month low of 8.9% in August.
